clue.text: Request place to be given to each

parts.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street addresses
EA is the usual abbreviation for each, as on price tags

explanation.surface: Someone asks that a seat be allotted to every guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest appeal, so it is a synonym for a request.

clue.text: Further appearance of 5 some heartlessly termed slack

parts.note: the answer to 5 Down appears again here, so its three letters are repeated

indicators.note: heartlessly means the word some loses its central letters, keeping only its two ends

explanation.surface: A wordy remark about a word turning up again, describing certain language as lax.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 5 Down is LOO; 'some heartlessly' leaves S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose and slack are synonyms for something not held tight.

clue.text: Admit top missing from equipment currently on shelf

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another comes before it, so the pieces run in clue order
in a down clue the top is the first letter, so the word for equipment loses its opening letter

parts.note: tack is the riding equipment for a horse: saddle, bridle and so on
now means at present, currently
a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that the uppermost item has gone from the gear presently stored on a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack is horse-riding gear; without its top it gives ACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge something is to admit or concede that it is true.

clue.text: Line subsequently adopted in fuel asset

indicators.note: adopted in means taken into, so the first pieces go inside the word for fuel

parts.note: coal is a fuel
later means subsequently

explanation.surface: A financial note about a line of fuel being taken up as an asset later.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is property pledged as security for a loan, an asset put up as guarantee.

clue.text: Carbon promoted by nuclear installation designer

indicators.note: in a down clue promoted means moved up, so the carbon letter shifts to the top of the word

parts.note: a reactor is the core installation of a nuclear power station
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Carbon is given prominence by the person who designed a nuclear plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The C in REACTOR moves up to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A creator is one who devises or makes something, a designer.

clue.text: Curtailment of diver's facilities

indicators.note: curtailment means cutting off the tail, so the last letter of the bird's name is dropped

parts.note: a loon is a diving bird, called a diver in Britain

explanation.surface: A diver's amenities have been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: The divers are birds, not swimmers: the loon (in Britain the great northern diver).
explanation.definitionFit: Loo is British slang for a toilet; 'the facilities' is a polite euphemism for the same thing.

clue.text: Mounts donkey, keeping colt to last

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the donkey word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
C is the abbreviation for colt in horse-racing form guides
the end is the last part

explanation.surface: A rider gets on a donkey, holding back the young horse till the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to climb or go up, so ascends is a synonym for mounts.

clue.text: Watercourse in the Skerries

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words the Skerries, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A stream to be found among the Skerries, a group of small islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Skerries are small rocky islets; the Esk is the name of several British rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Esk is a river, one example of a watercourse, in Scotland and England.

clue.text: Horse loves it, after shock

indicators.note: after says the pieces for loves and it follow the word for shock

parts.note: to appal is to shock
love is zero in tennis, and O looks like zero, so two loves are OO
SA, sex appeal, is 'it' in old slang

explanation.surface: A horse is fond of something after a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: The Appaloosa is a spotted breed of horse developed in North America.

clue.text: Wayward Romeo, with chick, exaggerating virility?

indicators.note: wayward means going astray, so the letters of the two words wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A wandering Romeo with a girl friend, putting on a show of machismo.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayward shuffles ROMEO and CHICK together.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock-heroic writing inflates a trivial subject with grand epic style; the question mark admits that exaggerated manliness is just one instance of this.

clue.text: Special headgear? Some take pictures

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wearing distinctive hats, a few photographers snap away.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a peaked French military cap, a particular kind of hat.

clue.text: Part of England not acceptable? Not acceptable, and that's genuine

indicators.note: not here strips the word for acceptable out of the county name

parts.note: Devon is a county of south-west England
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'
out means not acceptable, unfashionable

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a region of England is beyond the pale, and means it.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is an English county; 'not on' is a British idiom for unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Devout means sincere and earnest, as in a devout wish, so genuine fits.

clue.text: British mountain peak not foremost place for navigational equipment

indicators.note: not foremost means the front letter of the peak word is removed

parts.note: a pinnacle is a high pointed peak

explanation.surface: A British summit is not the leading spot for a ship's instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: A binnacle is the stand or housing on a ship's deck that holds the compass.

clue.text: By importing lager, finally we're stirring drinks provider

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the shuffled letters go inside the word by
finally takes the last letter of lager
stirring means mixing, so the letters of we're are mixed up

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped to give the letters of we're

explanation.surface: Bringing in lager, we end up stirring the pot for a drinks supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewery makes and supplies beer, so it provides drinks.

clue.text: A nasty blemish is found in trademark — one's not looking one's best with it

definitions.text: one's not looking one's best with it

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace, a blemish

indicators.note: found in means placed within, so is goes inside the trademark abbreviation

explanation.surface: A brand logo carries an ugly flaw, and the brand looks worse for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'looking': a person with the condition literally does not see at their best.
explanation.definitionFit: Astigmatism is an eye defect that blurs vision, so a sufferer does not see as well as they could.

clue.text: Carol sells shifts resembling T-shirts?

indicators.note: shifts means moves around, so the letters of the two words change places

explanation.surface: Carol sells shift dresses that look like T-shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like a noun for dresses in the surface but is the verb that rearranges CAROL SELLS.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shirt has no collar, so a garment like one is lacking a neckband; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Racing boat a stimulus for the Dark Blues?

parts.note: Oxford University's colour is dark blue, so its rowing crew are the Dark Blues: OU
a trigger is something that sets off an action, a stimulus

explanation.surface: A racing boat might spur on the Oxford crew.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Boat Race, Oxford are the Dark Blues and Cambridge the Light Blues.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrigger is a light racing rowing boat with rowlocks on brackets projecting from the sides.

clue.text: Twisting spoils piece of equipment

indicators.note: twisting means turning round, so the word for spoils is read backwards

parts.note: loot is plunder, spoils

explanation.surface: Bending something wrecks a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' looks like a verb meaning ruins, but it is the noun meaning plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool is an implement, a hand-held piece of equipment.

clue.text: Mostly pay attention to boss

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to study something is to pay close attention to it

explanation.surface: Advice to listen, largely, to the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like the employer but is the knob sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield or ceiling.

clue.text: Articles about old record, one produced by religious expert

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two articles wrap round the next pieces

parts.note: the and an are the definite and indefinite articles
a log is a record, as a ship's log
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Pieces of writing about an old document, one of them produced by a scholar of religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' covers both the definite and the indefinite article, which split to wrap round the middle pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A theologian is a specialist in the study of God and religious belief.

clue.text: Arguments about Arab customs

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the quarrels word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: tiffs are petty quarrels
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: Quarrels over the traditions of Arab people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'customs' is not traditions but duties levied at a border.
explanation.definitionFit: Tariffs are duties charged on imports, which is what customs means in the trade sense.

clue.text: Note that is penned in Church season, allowing freedom?

indicators.note: penned in means enclosed, so the note and that-is pieces sit inside the church season

parts.note: Lent is the season of fasting before Easter
ie is the abbreviation for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A note written during Lent about allowing freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lenient is tolerant and permissive, letting others off rather than restricting them.

clue.text: Story almost — almost — without digressions?

indicators.note: the first almost means the word for story loses its last letter

parts.note: a lie is a story, a falsehood
nearly means almost

explanation.surface: A storyteller stumbles, nearly saying something, as if keeping to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'almost' does two jobs: the first trims LIE to LI, the second is NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceeding in a straight line, step by step, is to go on without wandering off the subject.

clue.text: Subtlety is absent in bore?

indicators.note: absent in means missing from, so is is taken out of the bore word

parts.note: a nuisance is a bore, a pest

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a tedious person lacks finesse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine shade of meaning, a subtle distinction.

clue.text: Army boss, seizing US city, turning pessimistic

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the boss abbreviation holds the city inside it

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief

indicators.note: turning means the city abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: A military chief captures an American city and becomes gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic doubts people's motives; used attributively the noun means distrustful and gloomy in outlook.

clue.text: Offensive, unfeeling, lousy, heartless

indicators.note: heartless means each of the two words loses its middle, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A list of insults for a cruel, rotten and callous person.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can mean unpleasant or hostile, as in an ugly mood or ugly remarks.

clue.text: Certainly English used in description of teen fiction?

indicators.note: used in means put inside, so the English abbreviation goes within the fiction label

parts.note: YA, Young Adult, is the publishing label for teenage fiction

explanation.surface: Definitely English is used in labelling novels for teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yea is an old word for yes, used as an emphatic indeed or truly.

clue.text: Perforation, with central piece removed, ruined early keyboard instrument

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the middle letter of the eleven-letter word is taken out

explanation.surface: A hole punched in the middle spoiled a historic keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: PERFORATION has eleven letters; its sixth is R, leaving PERFOATION to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortepiano is the eighteenth-century forerunner of the modern piano.

clue.text: Regret being harsh, expelling daughter

indicators.note: expelling means throwing out, so the daughter letter is removed

parts.note: rude can mean harsh or rough
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent is sorry for being hard on a daughter and throwing her out.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it bitterly.

clue.text: 'Minor highway that man included in collection': newspaper

parts.note: a B road is a secondary road in Britain, below an A road

indicators.note: included in means put inside, so the pronoun goes within the word for collection

parts.note: a set is a collection
he is that man

explanation.surface: A headline about a man's minor road appearing in a compilation.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are classed A (major) and B (minor), so a minor highway is a B road.

clue.text: Millions associated with top-level club

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
ace means first-rate, top-level

explanation.surface: Huge sums of money linked with an elite football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is not a team but a heavy stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy club with a spiked or flanged head, a weapon.
